channel.title: IngestThis
channel.description: Articles, tutorials, and resources for Data Engineers, Scientists, Analysts, and Architects.

item.title: Agentic Data Architecture
item.description: A six-layer reference architecture for agents on company data: planners, tool boundaries, identity, the semantic layer, and what breaks when a layer is missing.

item.title: Running Apache Polaris in Production
item.description: Apache Polaris past the quickstart: persistence backends, realm bootstrap, replica token signing, upgrades, backups, and which failures take the lakehouse offline.

item.title: What the 2026 Consolidation Means for Open Formats
item.description: Tabular, Dremio, and a wave of data platform acquisitions: what changes for teams building on open formats and which guarantees survive a change of ownership.

item.title: Context Engineering for Data Agents
item.description: Why text-to-SQL accuracy collapses on enterprise schemas, the five kinds of context an agent needs, where each one hides, and how to make the semantics legible.

item.title: Guardrails for AI on Company Data
item.description: The control surfaces that actually contain damage once an agent is fooled: identity, permissions, audit trails, and prompt injection at the query layer.

item.title: Migrating Into Iceberg Without Moving Data
item.description: add_files, snapshot, and migrate compared: the three in-place paths into Iceberg, the reconciliation each requires, the layout traps, and the rollback story.

item.title: What Iceberg Table Maintenance Actually Costs
item.description: A cost model for compaction, snapshot expiry, orphan cleanup, and manifest rewriting: what each operation spends, on which meter, and how to set a schedule.

item.title: Running an Iceberg Lakehouse on Kubernetes
item.description: Catalog, maintenance, and compaction as Kubernetes workloads: scheduling classes, job structure, credential flow, and the failures that come from the interaction.

item.title: Partition Statistics Files in Apache Iceberg
item.description: The underused Iceberg metadata for planning: what the partition statistics file holds, what the spec guarantees, how to write one, and when it earns its slot.

item.title: What to Assert When You Test an Iceberg Pipeline
item.description: Fixtures, in-memory catalogs, and golden metadata: the assertions that catch wrong rows, unsafe reruns, schema drift, and concurrent-write corruption in CI.

item.title: The 2026 Iceberg REST Catalog Compatibility Report
item.description: A repeatable test for what an Iceberg REST catalog actually serves, a scoring scheme that separates design from breakage, and the 2026 evidence across seven catalogs.

item.title: Serving Iceberg Tables From Two Regions
item.description: Three multi-region topologies that work and one that mostly does not, what an Iceberg commit costs across regions, and where the catalog has to live.

item.title: How Iceberg Catalogs Hand Engines Storage Access
item.description: Credential vending end to end: the wire protocol, scoped access on each cloud, remote signing, credential lifetime on long jobs, and failures that look like bugs.

item.title: Kafka Connect to Iceberg: How the Commit Actually Works
item.description: Exactly-once semantics in the Iceberg sink connector: the coordinator, the control topic, offsets stored inside Iceberg snapshots, and where duplicates still get in.

item.title: What a Query Costs
item.description: Four meters, their real proportions, and how to attribute compute to a query, a table, and a team so a platform can answer what a dashboard costs to run.

item.title: The Open Lakehouse Explained, Then Built on Your Laptop with Dremio and MinIO
item.description: The five layers of the open lakehouse explained, then a lab: Parquet, Iceberg, Polaris, Arrow, and Ossie running in two containers on your own machine.

item.title: Where Lock-In Went
item.description: The format war ended and exit cost did not: where lock-in relocated after open tables won, how to measure it, and which costs are worth keeping down.

item.title: Data Quality Tooling Compared: Great Expectations, Soda, dbt Tests, and Anomaly Detection
item.description: A comparison of Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests, and anomaly detection, and a layered design that uses each where it fits.

item.title: The Data Team of the Agentic Era: Generalists Owning End-to-End Workflows
item.description: The case for generalists owning end-to-end data workflows with agents, the counterargument, and how to make the transition work.

item.title: dbt on Iceberg: Incremental Models on Open Tables
item.description: How dbt incremental materializations map to Iceberg operations, and the configuration, predicates, and maintenance that keep them healthy.
